requirements.requirement: Node1 has an enabled, persistent host firewall enforcing the requested policy across restart.
requirements.summary: Firewalld is enabled and active. The permanent and runtime rich rules survived a node1 reboot with a changed boot identity, and post-reboot traffic tests confirmed the policy still operated.

requirements.requirement: SSH to node1 is allowed from any address.
requirements.summary: The active public zone allows the SSH service, sshd listens on IPv4 and IPv6, and both node2 and node3 reached node1's SSH authentication stage after the restarts. The authentication failures show transport and firewall access succeeded, not that SSH was blocked.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is allowed from node2.
requirements.summary: The higher-precedence permanent rule accepts node2's address 10.100.94.11/32, and node2 received HTTP 200 from a confirmed listener on node1:9000 both before and after node1's reboot and again after all node restarts.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is rejected from node3 and every other source.
requirements.summary: A source-independent lower-precedence catch-all reject rule covers TCP/9000 after the node2-specific exception. Direct node3 attempts failed against a confirmed listener before and after node1's reboot and after all node restarts; the rule remained in runtime and permanent configuration.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1's persistent firewalld policy preserves unrestricted SSH access, accepts TCP/9000 only from node2's IPv4 address, and rejects other TCP/9000 sources. Direct behavior and persistence were demonstrated across reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong for all three nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services and networking.
limitations: Direct TCP/9000 rejection behavior was sampled from node3 rather than from every possible external address; universal rejection is established by the source-independent catch-all rule plus that representative test.

The lifecycle inventory does not inspect SSH known_hosts files, so retention of the two added entries is inferred from the commands' explicit “Permanently added” output and lack of cleanup rather than a final filesystem observation.
Operational hygiene cited unknown evidence IDs: cmd-107a989e75d0465

operational_hygiene.summary: The firewall mutation was necessary, temporary HTTP listeners and files were removed, final snapshots show no test listener, failed services, temporary test artifacts, or package damage, and all three required restart protocols were completed. Two minor unnecessary retained mutations occurred: SSH tests added node1's host key to node3's known_hosts and later to node2's known_hosts, with no evidence of removal (cmd-dfc269af2f6342f5 and cmd-a42ad92a70244656). The malformed initial node2 curl test also issued redundant requests and temporary server-log writes; those logs were subsequently removed, so it left no observed residue (cmd-107a989e75d0465, cmd-944cddbecf9649e2).
